must_fix_before_or_at_merge.issue: FD_SCRUB breaks under dash (Ubuntu /bin/sh, i.e. the ubuntu-latest CI runner that runs `make test` -> ai-godot). dash cannot parse `exec N>&-` for N >= 10 ('exec: 12: not found', shell exits 127). Reproduced locally with /bin/dash and fds 5,12,13 open: rc=127 and the service never starts; bash/macOS sh: ok. Whether Godot on Linux holds an fd >= 10 at spawn is unverified but likely (epoll, pck, pipes), so test_stub_session and every fake-service test could fail only in CI.
must_fix_before_or_at_merge.suggestion: Spawn via /bin/bash is not guaranteed either; instead close fds with a form dash accepts (eval "exec $n>&-" fails for 2-digit n in dash; use `/bin/sh -c` -> `python`-free alternatives: loop `exec {n}>&-` is bash-only), or avoid a shell: set FD_CLOEXEC on Godot's pipe ends is not exposed, so the portable fix is a tiny AILANG/ailang-side or `env`-free wrapper, or run the scrub under `bash` when present and assert/skip with an explicit message otherwise. Re-verify on the real CI run before relying on this milestone.

must_fix_before_or_at_merge.issue: Relaxed frame check hides intermittent blocking. Mutants I added: `if randi()%25==0: OS.delay_msec(10)` (4% of polls) and a 30 ms sleep on 1-in-40 BUSY polls both SURVIVED the full --faults suite under load (2.5/core). Only a per-poll block (5 ms every poll) was caught.
must_fix_before_or_at_merge.suggestion: Under load keep a tighter tail rule (e.g. 99% < 2 ms is too noisy, so instead use p50 < 1 ms plus none >= 20 ms), and add a deterministic non-timing check: spy on the bridge (counter of OS.delay_msec-like waits is impossible), so assert structurally that poll() contains no delay/wait_for_task_completion outside shutdown; or run the strict check with `nice`/idle detection and fail CI if it could not run strict.

non_blocking_findings.issue: Vacuous: with the `_kill()` removed from `_timeout()` the check still passed (the hang child is gone by then, or the pid probe is satisfied), and only the later 'next request relaunches at once' cascade failed. A timeout that forgets to kill is not caught by its own check. Confirms deviation 7 and shows the executor's mutant row targets the cascade only.
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: Check the pid is dead immediately after the timeout outcome (poll until child_gone within ~500 ms) with a service that cannot exit on its own (e.g. /bin/sleep 30 as in test_shutdown_grace).

deviation_verdicts.1_frame_bound_relaxed_under_load: Acceptable in principle, weak in practice: it catches per-poll blocking but misses intermittent blocks up to 49 ms on <=5% of polls (two survivors). Observed worst polls under load were 8-12 ms, so the relaxation is real. Needs a structural or tighter-tail check (F2). No evidence the shipped code blocks: poll() has no waits, spawn/kill are on WorkerThreadPool, drains are capped at 16 chunks.
deviation_verdicts.2_workerthreadpool_thread_safety: Sound. The spawn task writes only `_spawned` and is read after is_task_completed/wait_for_task_completion; kill lambdas capture only an int pid; all signals, queues and phase state are touched on the main thread in poll()/request(); shutdown joins spawn and kill tasks. No race found.
deviation_verdicts.3_fd_scrub_wrapper: Correct on macOS (sh is bash-compatible; /dev/fd listing works; pid preserved via exec, test confirms the child's extra fds contain no PIPE). NOT portable: dash (Ubuntu CI) fails for fds >= 10 with rc 127 (F1). Confirm on a real ubuntu run. SimBridge has the same exposure and is unfixed.
deviation_verdicts.4_timeouts_count_in_window_no_backoff: Acceptable and consistent with design lines 357-360 (timeout restarts lazily; 3 failures in 10 min disables). Note _consecutive still increments so a later crash after timeouts gets a longer backoff; tested indirectly only.
deviation_verdicts.5_stub_launch_only: Acceptable for AI.6; exported path untested, must be covered by AI.7/AI.9 before release.
deviation_verdicts.6_fake_service_not_in_exports: Acceptable; it is a test tool, exports govern shipped modules.
deviation_verdicts.7_kill_mutant_caught_by_cascade: Not acceptable as stated: the dedicated kill assertion is vacuous (see non-blocking finding 1). Cheap fix.
